diagram.title: Small errors need a scale-aware budget
diagram.prediction: Why can a larger absolute difference pass at a larger reference value?
diagram.reading: Each table row is one elementwise tolerance check: allowed difference is \(2\times10^{-6}+2\times10^{-5}|y|\). Near zero, a difference of \(10^{-6}\) passes and \(3\times10^{-6}\) fails; at reference 100, the budget is 0.002002, so 0.001 passes. These are hand-worked tolerance examples. The executed plot separately shows the epsilon fault’s first mismatch at normalization.
diagram.alt: Read each row as one elementwise decision using absolute tolerance \(2\times10^{-6}\) and relative tolerance \(2\times10^{-5}\). Near zero the absolute term determines the allowance. At reference \(100\), the relative term increases it. These are hand-worked tolerance examples, not measured conversion errors; the executed bar plot below reports the model comparison.
